interpretation_notes_markdown:
## Changes justified by the expanded evidence

| Previous boundary | Decision | Evidence and reason |
|---|---|---|
| G1 official explanation / G2 external interpretation | Replace with G1 explanatory accounts, G2 process/access guidance, G3 catalogues/metadata. Record provenance separately. | Waterloo publishes consultant studies, municipal summaries, instructions and source lists. Authorship does not distinguish their information role: an outside consultant’s technical assessment belongs in B3, while an independent oversight finding belongs in E3/B3. Official summaries and external explainers can both be G1. |
| E3 monitoring focused on performance/progress | Expand to monitoring, disclosure and oversight. | Conflict declarations, expenses, lobbying records and independent investigations are accountability information without necessarily measuring delivery performance. The narrower wording did not describe them adequately. |
| D3 “subsequent status” | Rename effect, conditions and review status. | A notice can establish commencement/conditions/appeal status at the same time it announces a determination. “Subsequent” incorrectly suggests all status arises later. |
| B2 applications | Clarify cases, applications and solicitations. | An administrative request persists across stages; procurement also publishes requests and determinations. A guide or blank form is kept in G2, not treated as a completed case. |
| F2 service context | Make asset context explicit; F3 distinguishes measured and modelled conditions. | Facility inventories, infrastructure-condition evidence and projections need a clear place without calling them decisions or treating projections as observations. |
| C1 opportunities/conditions and C2 contributions received | Broaden to C1 participation arrangements/opportunities and C2 participation records/contributions; retain C3 synthesis/response. | The water-plan consultation appendix contains outreach lists and completed sign-in sheets as well as notices and comments. Neither an intended recipient nor an attendee can automatically be treated as having expressed a view. |
| A, B1/B3 and D1/D2 distinctions | Retain with clarified wording. | The new sources continue to separate framework, requested action, evidence, proceedings and determination. No new broad category was necessary. |

The revised G categories are a functional improvement, not a judgment that official/external provenance is unimportant. Authority/publisher and access state are now explicit table fields. E3 is not a catch-all: it requires a tracking, disclosure or oversight function.

The relevant evidence is directly exposed in the [City technical-submission library](https://www.waterloo.ca/planning-and-development/manuals-guidelines-and-standards/terms-of-reference-for-development-applications/), [Regional accountability collection](https://www.regionofwaterloo.ca/government-and-council/transparency-and-accountability/), [City asset-management collection](https://www.waterloo.ca/council-and-city-administration/budget-and-financial-reports/asset-management/) and the linked records in the inventory. The amendments above are classification judgments drawn from those differences, not requirements added to the challenge.

For the participation amendment, the [water-plan consultation appendix, PDF pp.2–3 and 45–46](https://media-002-ca.cdn.govstack.com/waterloo-013-ca/media/afgd4m05/water-distribution-master-plan-appendix-4.pdf) explicitly organizes notification, contacts, attendance, display material and contributions. The [post-review compilation, PDF pp.1–2](https://media-002-ca.cdn.govstack.com/waterloo-013-ca/media/nyjfweb4/water-distribution-master-plan-comments-received-through-community-feedback.pdf) relates comments to actions/status. These are historical process records, not current invitations.

### How to interpret overlapping categories

The hierarchy groups **information by its role**, not by subject, file format or website folder. A single publication can combine institutional authority and an operative rule (A1/A2), measurements and their interpretation (F3/B3), intended action and delivery planning (A3/E2), or a determination and its current effect (D2/D3). Participation inputs and a synthesis can also share a publication (C2/C3); the original contributions are not thereby identical to the municipality's summary. These are deliberate overlaps, not competing claims that one physical file belongs in only one place.

Some particulars are narrower subject families; others are components or containers. Waterloo itself publishes at these different levels. An appendix is not automatically a new substantive category, and a whole library is not equivalent to one record. The tables explicitly describe that level, rather than presenting the row count as a count of mutually exclusive or uniquely standardized document types.

### Terms used in this supplement

- A **bylaw** is a municipal legal enactment; a **resolution** is a formally adopted motion. A proposed enactment or recommendation is distinct from its adoption.
- **Delegation of authority** assigns power to another body or official. A public **delegation** can also mean a person addressing a meeting; that is a different use of the word.
- **Terms of reference (TOR)** define a committee's mandate or a required study's scope, depending on context. They are not the committee's decisions or the completed study.
- An **Official Plan** governs land-use planning; a **strategic plan** states organizational priorities. An **Official Plan amendment (OPA)** changes the former.
- A **schedule** can be an attached map, table or set of clauses; in transit it can mean a timetable. **Consent** in a planning application and consent business on an agenda are different processes.
- **FOI** means a formal freedom-of-information request. It is an access route, with disclosure determined under applicable rules, not a promise of release.
- **FIR** is Ontario's Financial Information Return. **GTFS** is the General Transit Feed Specification and **GBFS** the General Bikeshare Feed Specification. Their technical formats differ from municipal reporting obligations.

## Access and transferability labels

| Access label | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Read | Substantive page/record or collection contents inspected during this research or the earlier same-date investigation. If the URL is a collection, this does not mean all child files were read. |
| Listed | A specific published item/type and link were observed in an inspected collection. Child contents were not independently audited in this pass. |
| Metadata | Schema/description inspected; substantive dataset rows not retrieved. |
| Data | Actual small record/count response retrieved in the earlier same-date tests. Does not mean complete extraction. |
| Mixed | Some contents/links work, while relevant components fail or remain unverified. The row states the difference. |
| Request | Publisher describes a contact/request route; substantive record not obtained. |

| Transfer label | What can be inferred |
|---|---|
| C | A comparable record family is evidenced in other examined municipalities. Exact subtype, naming, fields, coverage and access can differ. |
| O | Dependent on an Ontario institutional/legal process; do not assume the same mechanism in other provinces or every municipality. |
| P | Potentially transferable where the relevant service/project exists; no type-by-type cross-municipality verification claimed. |
| L | A local scheme, branded publication, geography or organizational split needs local interpretation. This does not mean no analogous information exists elsewhere. |
| T | A documented technical feed specification applies to the advertised resource. Actual conformance/completeness was not audited; adoption is conditional, not universal. |
| T-O | A standardized Ontario reporting family/template, not a Canada-wide municipal document system. Filing availability still varies by municipality/year. |

Compound labels preserve both findings: **O/C** means an Ontario-dependent family with a verified comparable counterpart; **C/P** means the broad family recurs but the exact subtype was not individually compared; **L/P** means the local publication has a role that could have an analogue. The comparison section supplies the evidence and limits behind these labels. **No finding establishes that every municipality publishes all this information in the same way.**

A: Establishes who may act and what governs municipal action, rather than what happened in a particular case.

A1: Organization, responsibilities, delegations and procedures for exercising power. Institutional rules belong here even when published as a policy or bylaw.
A2: Applicable requirements, permissions, prohibitions and legally operative conditions. A draft standard is not classified as already operative merely because it appears in an official document.
A3: Objectives, priorities, plans and assessment principles. Some have legal force; the distinction from A2 is their planning/guiding role, not an assumption that policy is optional.

B: Matters under consideration and supporting evidence
Establishes what is being sought or considered and the evidence offered for assessing it; separates the proposal and its case from an authoritative determination.

B1: The unit presented for consideration and action requested of a decision-making body. Agenda placement does not establish acceptance.
B2: An identifiable request or solicitation moving through an administrative process. The case can exist independently of a particular meeting and need not end at Council.
B3: Reasoning, baseline evidence, alternatives, projections, reviews and technical analysis used to assess a matter. Publication does not settle the truth or acceptance of each analytical claim.

C: Distinguishes arrangements and opportunities, actual participation and input, and the institution’s interpretation or response.

C1: How participation is organized, including outreach/notification arrangements, scope, eligibility, timing and channels. A contact list does not establish attendance, and a post announcing an outcome is not automatically a current opportunity.
C2: Records of actual participation and substantive input as supplied. Attendance and an expressed opinion are different things. A blank form, empty agenda heading or advertised question tool does not demonstrate that actual participation or contributions were obtained.
C3: How input was grouped, interpreted, answered or represented in municipal reasoning. A synthesis is distinct from original submissions and does not by itself prove causal influence.

D: Separates the conduct of decision-making, the authoritative action, and the action’s effect/status.

D1: What occurred within a meeting or hearing, including procedural context. Draft status and source limitations remain part of interpreting the record.
D2: An authorized body or official exercising power. A published summary of the act and evidence of completed delivery are different records.
D3: Applicability, commencement, conditions, finality and review/appeal state at a particular time. This information may be issued with a decision, not only later.

E: Distinguishes financial resources, practical execution, and observation/disclosure/oversight of action.

E1: Financial requirements, allocations, commitments, projections and actuals. Those states must be distinguished even within one publication.
E2: Planned or actual execution and operational progress. A plan, award, permit and completed undertaking establish different things.
E3: Tracking performance and follow-through, public accountability disclosures, and independent scrutiny. Disclosing a potential conflict is not a finding of wrongdoing.

F: Descriptive context for interpreting relevance and effects. Context does not automatically establish legal applicability or causal impact.

F1: Location, shape, boundaries and geographic relationships. Operative spatial rules also receive A2/A3 where warranted.
F2: What services/assets exist or are intended, whom they serve, and operational arrangements. Performance measurements additionally belong in E3/F3.
F3: Quantified conditions and patterns, including estimates/projections when labelled. Distinguishes observations from future modelling and both from causal claims.

G: Groups publications by their communicative function. Authorship and publisher are recorded separately, rather than deciding the category.

G1: Interpretive accounts intended to make a matter understandable. Official and external accounts can both perform this function; neither is automatically the underlying decision instrument.
G2: Instructions, eligibility explanations, submission requirements and ways to participate or obtain information. The guide is different from the completed record it describes.
G3: Descriptions and navigation that help locate substantive information. A linked resource, empty listing or schema is not equivalent to having retrieved its contents.

R1: One source establishes who may act or which rules/policies apply. Legal requirements and advisory planning direction must retain their different force.
R2: submitted to; considered in; receives; records a disposition
Connects stages or institutional handling of a matter. A later stage is conditional: matters can change, stop, branch or use delegated authority.
R3: supports; assesses; summarizes; reviews; responds to analysis
Connects information with reasoning or scrutiny. A review does not prove acceptance, a summary does not reproduce every input, and support does not establish causation.
R4: enacts; amends; approves; commences; is subject to review
Connects an authorized act to a continuing rule or its effect/conditions/status. Adoption, approval, commencement and finality can differ.
R5: informs a funding request; allocates; schedules; implements
Connects direction, resources and practical execution. A plan is not automatically funded and an award or budget is not proof of completion.
R6: monitors; discloses; investigates; may prompt a response
Connects action/proceedings with performance, disclosure or oversight. A conflict declaration is not a finding of misconduct; findings and imposed consequences are distinct.
R7: links to; cites; identifies; locates; matches by identifier
Connects records through published URLs, identifiers or catalogue entries. A reconstructed match must be distinguished from an explicit link, and navigation does not confer substantive access.
R8: Connects an explanatory account to the underlying matter or records it describes. An accessible explanation can omit conditions and does not replace the authoritative record.
